subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Combined-rate, alternate-day, efficiency comparison, men-women-children, partial work

questions.stem: A can complete a piece of work in 10 days, B can do the same in 15 days. Together they will finish the work in:
questions.explanation: Rate of A = 1/10 work/day; B = 1/15. Combined = 1/10 + 1/15 = (3 + 2)/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 per day. Time = 6 days. LCM shortcut: take LCM(10, 15) = 30 units of work; A does 3 u/day, B does 2 u/day → together 5 u/day → 30/5 = 6 days. Standard combined-work formula: T = (T_A · T_B) / (T_A + T_B) = (10·15)/(10+15) = 150/25 = 6.

questions.stem: If 6 men and 8 women can complete a work in 10 days, while 26 men and 48 women can finish the same in 2 days. Time taken by 15 men + 20 women is:
questions.explanation: Let 1 man-day = m work, 1 woman-day = w work. Equation 1: (6m + 8w) × 10 = 1 → 60m + 80w = 1. Equation 2: (26m + 48w) × 2 = 1 → 52m + 96w = 1. Equate: 60m + 80w = 52m + 96w → 8m = 16w → m = 2w. Substitute: 60(2w) + 80w = 1 → 200w = 1 → w = 1/200, m = 1/100. Now (15m + 20w) per day = 15/100 + 20/200 = 0.15 + 0.1 = 0.25 = 1/4 → time = 4 days.

questions.stem: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days; B alone in 30 days. How long will A alone take?
questions.explanation: Let A alone take x days. Combined rate = 1/12 per day. B = 1/30. So 1/x + 1/30 = 1/12 → 1/x = 1/12 − 1/30 = (5 − 2)/60 = 3/60 = 1/20 → x = 20 days.

questions.stem: A and B can complete a job in 8 days. They worked together for 4 days, then B left. A finished the rest of the work in 6 more days. How long would A alone take to finish the entire job?
questions.explanation: In 4 days together: 4/8 = 1/2 work done. Remaining 1/2 done by A alone in 6 days → A's rate = (1/2)/6 = 1/12 per day → A alone takes 12 days. Verify: A's rate = 1/12; combined rate = 1/8; so B's rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = (3 − 2)/24 = 1/24 → B alone 24 days ✓.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: If A is twice as efficient as B, and together they complete a work in 12 days, how long will B take alone?
questions.explanation: Let B's rate = r → A's rate = 2r. Combined = 3r per day. Together complete in 12 days → 3r × 12 = 1 → r = 1/36. B alone = 1/r = 36 days. A alone = 1/(2r) = 18 days. Verify: 1/18 + 1/36 = 2/36 + 1/36 = 3/36 = 1/12 ✓.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 20 days respectively. They work on alternate days starting with A. The work is completed in:
questions.explanation: LCM of 12 and 20 = 60 units. A's rate = 60/12 = 5 u/day, B's rate = 60/20 = 3 u/day. In a 2-day cycle starting with A: A on day 1 (5 u) + B on day 2 (3 u) = 8 u per cycle. After 7 full cycles (14 days): 7 × 8 = 56 u done; 4 u remaining. Day 15 is A's turn → A does 5 u/day → needs 4/5 = 0.8 day. Total = 14 + 0.8 = 14.8 days.

questions.stem: A is 25% more efficient than B. If B takes 20 days to do a job alone, how many days will A alone take?
questions.explanation: If A is 25% MORE efficient, A's rate = 1.25 × B's rate. Time ∝ 1/rate, so A's time = B's time / 1.25 = 20/1.25 = 16 days. Cross-check: B takes 20 days; A's rate = 1.25 × (1/20) = 1/16 per day → 16 days for full work ✓.
